site.label: Store parameters: floor area, net usable share, stacking height, rent, and the derived capacity and daily rate

groups.label: Material group master: one row per material group with dimensions, quantity, price, replenishment settings and age profile

verticals.label: Vertical roll-up: sums of the material group rows by vertical, with the allocation and projection

cost.label: Cost split for the month: rent charged to stock, handling, utilities and the overflow store

siteOptions.label: Site options: the current unit and three alternatives on one comparison template

inbound.label: Commitments: stock mapped to purchase orders, free stock, and material in transit with its expected arrival

cbm.text: Cubic metres. The whole store is measured by volume, not pallet count. Unit CBM is length times breadth times height in metres, formed in whole cubic centimetres and rounded once to two decimals so a true half always rounds up; group CBM is unit CBM times quantity, exact.

capacity.text: Net usable floor area times the stacking height: 13,640 sq ft (62 percent of 22,000) is 1267.2 m2, times 3.9 m is 4942.08 CBM.

allocation.text: The share of capacity set aside for a vertical. Allocations sum to the store capacity. Idle CBM is allocation less stock held; a negative figure is stock over the allocation.

utilisation.text: Stock CBM (main store plus overflow) over allocated CBM, or over store capacity for the whole store, as a percentage to one decimal. The optimal band is 60 to 80 percent: below it space is paid for and unused, above it picking and put-away slow down.

rackable.text: A group that can be held on standard pallet racking. Non-rackable stock is floor stored or held at the overflow site, and it is the stock that consumes floor area fastest.

overflow.text: Third-party space rented by the CBM per day at AED 0.6, 2.6 times the store's own rate.

dailyRate.text: Annual rent over 365 days over capacity CBM: AED 418,000 over 365 over 4942.08 is AED 0.2317 per CBM per day.

dailyCost.text: For a group, main-store CBM times the daily rate plus overflow CBM times the overflow rate, rounded once to whole AED. For a vertical and for the store, the sum of its groups.

stockValue.text: Quantity times average unit price at cost, whole AED, per material group. Every higher figure is a sum.

ageBands.text: Stock value by days since receipt: under 90, 90 to 180, 180 to 365, over 365. The bands sum to stock value. CBM by band splits the group CBM in the same proportion.

avgAge.text: Value-weighted days since receipt, using the band midpoints 45, 135, 270 and 540 days.

turnover.text: Annualised issues at cost (twice the July to December forecast times unit price) over stock value. Higher is faster moving.

abc.text: Material groups ranked by stock value; A is the first 70 percent of value, B the next 20, C the last 10. Each class carries a storage rule.

safetyStock.text: The units held against demand variation and late delivery: ten to twenty-five days of forecast demand, set per group.

maxStock.text: Reorder point plus one order cycle of demand. The quantity an order tops the group up to.

leadTime.text: Days from purchase order to receipt at the store, per group, from supplier history.

demand.text: Units expected to issue in July to December 2026 (184 days). Demand per day is that figure over 184, to two decimals.

reorderPoint.text: Safety stock plus lead time times demand per day, rounded up. When stock falls to it, an order placed today arrives as safety stock is reached.

daysOfCover.text: Quantity over demand per day, rounded down. The projected stock-out date is the stock date plus days of cover. A group with no forecast demand has no days of cover and no stock-out date; it shows as healthy for ordering and as a slow mover for aging.

status.text: Below reorder point: quantity at or under the reorder point, order now. Within lead time: above the reorder point but days of cover within lead time plus 30 days, order this month. Healthy: neither.

mapped.text: Stock value already committed to a customer order. Free stock is stock value less that commitment.

inTransit.text: Ordered material not yet received, with its expected arrival date. Not counted in stock.

projection.text: Month-end CBM for the next four months, simulated day by day: each group falls by its demand per day and never below zero; material in transit lands on its expected date; an order for max stock less the balance is placed on the first day the balance is at or under the reorder point while nothing is on order, and lands one lead time in days later, in whatever month that day falls (a group already below on the stock date orders that day). Month-end CBM is unit CBM times the balance in whole units.

rentCharged.text: Main-store CBM times the daily rate times the days in the month, per group, rounded once. Rent for idle capacity is shown on its own line so the month adds to the actual rent, and the CBM column counts main-store CBM only so it adds to capacity; overflow CBM has its own column.

handling.text: Fixed: the storekeepers, split by CBM share. Variable: forecast issues in the month times AED 6 per movement.

effectiveRate.text: Monthly rent plus the one-off agent commission spread over a 36-month term, per sq ft per month. An option's annual rent is the sum of its parts, each an area at a rate; the commission is 5 percent of the rent on new space only.

precisionPolicy: Money is an integer in AED at the material-group level, rounded once: quantity times unit price for stock value, CBM times the daily rate for storage cost. Every vertical and store figure is a sum of those integers, so tables that show the same figure tie exactly.

CBM is rounded once to two decimals at the unit level (length times breadth times height) and once at the group level (unit CBM times quantity). Every higher CBM figure is a sum of those two-decimal figures, carried in hundredths, and the calculator in the browser applies the same rule from data/cbm.ts.
Percentages are one decimal from the sums, never from other percentages. Shares that must total 100.0 (ABC classes, value shares) are allocated by largest remainder.
Age bands, CBM by band, and the month cost allocations are integer splits by largest remainder, so each set sums exactly to its total.

Demand per day is the forecast over 184 days to two decimals; the reorder point rounds up; days of cover rounds down. Status derives from those three figures by the stated rule for every group, with no hand overrides.
Dates are calendar days from the stock date, 31 August 2026. Every timestamp is GST (Asia/Dubai, +04:00).
assumptions: Halvard Engineering Group is fictional. Every material group, brand, quantity, price, dimension and date is generated from one seed by scripts/generate_demo_data.ts. No real company, part number, supplier or site appears.

The central store holds the stocked material groups of the ten verticals. Project-site stock, service spares on vans and software licences carried as inventory in the division books are outside the store, so the store value sits below the division inventory line in the MIS.
Store parameters are chosen, not measured: 22,000 sq ft at AED 19 per sq ft per year, 62 percent net usable after aisles, docks and offices, 3.9 m usable stacking height.
Allocations by vertical are a planning split of capacity, not physical walls. One vertical over its allocation and one well under it are deliberate, to show what the pages do with each.
The overflow store is priced per CBM per day and holds only non-rackable items from three verticals. Its CBM counts in each vertical utilisation because the stock exists whether or not it fits.

Forecast demand is July to December 2026 by group. Lead times are supplier history by vertical. Safety stock is ten to twenty-five days of demand. These drive the reorder points shown; changing them in the generator changes every status.
The site options are illustrative: one current unit and three alternatives on the same comparison template. Rents and commissions are chosen figures.
The CBM calculator edits live only in the browser session. Reset restores the published figures. Nothing is saved and nothing is sent anywhere.

abc.rule: Prime storage: ground-level rack faces nearest dispatch, counted monthly.
Upper rack levels or the overflow store, counted at the annual stock take.
